A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same oscillation-based quantization work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable. Internal reporting inconsistencies in v2 do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 experiments, toy-model simulations, and analyses of oscillations, hyperparameters, and convergence.

after.justification: v2 retains original CIFAR-10 results and adds Tiny-ImageNet evaluations, statistical tests, and further sensitivity and layer analyses.

M1.justification: The layer-normalized quadratic regularizer and its STE gradient remain the same: v1 Eqs. 23–24 correspond to v2 Eqs. 19–20. Renaming OsciQuant to Oscillations and explaining the replacement of the toy model's input factor by lambda do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: v2 expands the CIFAR-10-only evaluation to Tiny-ImageNet, with ResNet-18 and Tiny ViT fine-tuning and target-bit and cross-bit evaluations in Tables 4–5. CIFAR-10 ternary evaluation remains present in Appendix A.3.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the full-precision/PTQ baseline and QAT. Tiny-ImageNet uses this same comparator set. Oscillations is the renamed proposed method, and newly cited oscillation-suppression methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Fine-tuning lambda changes from a stated value of 1 to bit-dependent values in {1, 0.75, 0.5}; unchanged CIFAR-10 scores do not establish reruns. Added protocols include 50-epoch Tiny-ImageNet fine-tuning and a full-data, pretrained ResNet lambda sweep. Table 6 also describes retained ternary results as 50-epoch fine-tuning, inconsistently with its from-scratch rows and the main setup.

E4.justification: v2 adds a broad logarithmic lambda sweep for pretrained ResNet-18 (Figure 5), ResNet convergence curves at two learning rates (Figure 9), and oscillation/weight-distribution comparisons across multiple layers (Figure 10). Earlier sensitivity and Tiny ViT convergence analyses remain. The counting-artifact diagnostic in v1 Appendix A.5 is removed.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Welch's t-tests, t-scores, and p-values for oscillation-count comparisons previously presented visually. Retained main CIFAR-10 results still report five-seed means and standard deviations. However, Tiny-ImageNet Tables 4 and 5 state three versus five runs, and relocated ternary Table 6 states three instead of v1's five; these reporting changes do not establish actual changes in runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial Tiny-ImageNet and supplementary results. Table 4 reports 3-bit ResNet accuracy of 49.34 ± 0.76 for Oscillations versus 54.08 ± 0.52 for QAT, exposing a gap on the added benchmark. Retained CIFAR-10 3/4-bit accuracies are unchanged, but mean training epochs and ternary-trained cross-bit numerical rows disappear. Table 6 changes the fine-tuned ResNet FP32 baseline from 88.50 ± 0.64 to 83.26 ± 1.07, conflicting with retained main tables.

T1.justification: v2 Eq. 18 removes v1 Eq. 22's asserted equality between the quantized loss and the heuristic regularized objective, retaining only the surrogate objective. The scalar and two-weight derivations are otherwise retained. The expanded oscillation definition restates the earlier counting rule, and the dampening interpretation adds no new proof.

C1.justification: The central claim that induced oscillations benefit quantization remains. However, v2 drops v1's introductory suggestion that oscillations capture all beneficial effects of QAT and qualifies the abstract's accuracy-recovery claim as holding in most cases, rather than broadly matching QAT at three bits and above.

C2.justification: v1 identifies additional effects in the two-weight model without explaining their role. v2 Section 6 and Appendix A.3 interpret the additional term as oscillation dampening and speculate that missing dampening explains the regularizer's ternary weakness. v2 explicitly emphasizes that oscillations alone do not capture full QAT dynamics and discusses the added Tiny-ImageNet shortfall. The earlier cross-bit early-stopping recommendation is removed.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies PTQ as direct weight quantization without calibration and supplies settings for the added experiments. The stated code repository changes from OsciQuant to osc_reg; availability is not verified. v2 omits the explicit no-data-augmentation statement, some oscillation-logging details, and reported mean training epochs.

R1.justification: v2 substantially narrows positioning toward oscillation mechanisms and suppression, removing discussions of robustness methods by Alizadeh and Chmiel, quantizer granularity, and multi-bit supernets. It adds Huang et al. on quantization variation and an explicit first-to-argue claim about oscillations being essential. Publication updates for the retained Li and Défossez papers are not new cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, preliminaries and related work are merged, and the toy analysis gains separate mechanism and clustering subsections. Results are reorganized by dataset, ternary treatment moves to an appendix, and limitations and broader-impact prose are added or rewritten. OsciQuant is renamed Oscillations throughout.

P2.justification: v2 merges the original CIFAR-10 accuracy tables into a model-column comparison, separates ternary results into Table 6, and removes epoch columns. It adds statistical and Tiny-ImageNet tables, redraws toy illustrations, expands appendix figures, and replaces the counting diagnostic with a multilayer display. Typography, captions, and figure placement are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: Tiny-ImageNet evaluation and broader lambda/layer analyses strengthen v1's CIFAR-10-only evidence and reveal additional applicability limits. v2 also more explicitly acknowledges the restricted scope of the toy-model explanation. The net gain is limited by inconsistent run counts and uncertainties in Tables 4–5, inconsistent baseline values in Table 6, captions overstating agreement with QAT, and removal of training-epoch and ternary cross-bit results.
